output.question: What are the details of Bayer's merger with Monsanto?
output.answer: Monsanto did not merge with Bayer. Bayer bought it outright. Bayer completed the purchase on June 7, 2018, paying Monsanto shareholders $128 per share in cash. Including Monsanto's debt as of Feb 28, 2018, the total cost was about $63 billion. Bayer first said it was interested in May 2016 and formally announced the $128-per-share deal in September 2016. The US Justice Department approved the deal on the condition that Bayer sell assets to BASF. Monsanto's shares were delisted from the NYSE, and Bayer stopped using Monsanto as a company name. The deal's biggest lasting effect has been the Roundup (glyphosate) litigation. On June 25, 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled 7-2 that federal pesticide law blocks state-law failure-to-warn claims. Separately, Bayer's Monsanto unit asked a Missouri judge on Sept 14, 2026 to grant final approval of a $7.25 billion class settlement. The judge has not ruled yet, and Bayer's CEO expects a decision before Christmas.

key_facts.fact: Bayer completed its acquisition of Monsanto on June 7, 2018. Monsanto shareholders were paid $128 per share.
Total cost was about $63 billion, including Monsanto's debt outstanding as of Feb 28, 2018.
Bayer first expressed interest in May 2016 and formally announced the $128-per-share deal in September 2016.
The DOJ approved the deal on conditions. Integration could begin only after Bayer completed the divestments to BASF. Monsanto stopped being a company name.

On June 25, 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled 7-2 that Bayer cannot be sued in state courts on failure-to-warn claims over Roundup. About 200,000 Roundup-related claims have been made against Bayer, and it previously set aside $16 billion.

On Sept 14, 2026, Bayer's Monsanto unit asked St. Louis Judge Timothy Boyer to approve a $7.25B Roundup settlement. Payouts would range from $10,000 to $165,000, and the judge did not say when he would rule.
Bayer CEO Bill Anderson expects the Missouri judge to rule on approval before Christmas.

caveats: This was an acquisition: Bayer bought Monsanto outright. It was not a merger of equals.
Bayer's own closing release (bayer.com) returned 403 when fetched, so the deal terms are cited from trade press (PharmTech) that reports Bayer's announcement.

As of the latest sources, the Missouri judge had not ruled on the $7.25B settlement, and the outcome may have changed since. More than 100 class members and some health plans objected, including to the $675M fee request.
The Supreme Court ruling covers failure-to-warn claims. Design-defect and other claims may still be possible.
The TradingView recap has no visible publication date, and its count of pending claims (~65,000) differs from AP's figure of ~200,000 total claims made.
